For bits to be distinct from one another, there must be relational non-identity among them, that *is* Space. A computation lacking any of the three is not a computation but something weaker: a static set of symbols (no Time), a dynamic flux with no being (no Substance), or a homogeneous stream with no distinguishable units (no Space). Landauer's [-@landauer1961] principle cuts the same way from physics: erasing a bit costs kT ln 2 of energy (the Landauer limit, where k is Boltzmann's constant and T is temperature, the minimum thermodynamic cost of erasing one bit), and thermodynamic cost requires a physical substrate with temporal evolution, spatial distinctness of states, and persistent beings.

A kindred deflation drops the computational framing entirely for ontic structural realism: @ladymanRoss2007 argue that only relational structure is fundamental and relata are ontologically dispensable. Structure, on this view, goes all the way down, with no bearer beneath it. This form of the inversion has to be met head-on rather than deflected, because the case against it is the case for Φ.

Structure is not a thing; structure is what things have. A pattern is always a pattern *of* something, as ownership is always ownership *of* something and a dent is always a dent *in* something. "Structure all the way down" asks us to keep the having while dismissing everything that has: to keep the floor plan after demolishing the building. But the structure of a building is not a second object standing alongside it; subtract the building and no structure is left over, only a blueprint, and a blueprint is a *description* of a building rather than a building.

The structural realist has a reply: the relata are nothing but nodes in the structure. A "thing" just is a position in the pattern, with no nature of its own. But a node is still a something. To be a position is to be the position *of* something positioned; relocating the bearer into the word "node" does not abolish it, it renames it. Nor does multiple realizability help: that one structure can be built in steel, wood, or concrete shows it independent of any *particular* material, not independent of material *as such*. A blueprint realizable in many media is still a sheet of paper until it is built in some medium or other. The dispute reduces to a single question: can anything be *exhausted* by its relations, with no nature of its own beneath how it relates? If not, then under every structure there is at least a minimal what-it-is that the structure is the structure *of*, and that is Φ. This is the intrinsic nature Russellian monism locates beneath physical structure ([§4.3.3](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-3)), and it is the precise point on which the present account parts from the structuralism of [§4.3.9](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-9). Relational structure without anything across which relations obtain is ∅ (the Null State, the configuration in which none of T, S, or Φ is instantiated), foreclosed in [§2.7](the-argument.html#sec-2-7).

*The Concession Move.* One last move remains to the opponent: not denial, but concession, that information is the substrate, and what the argument calls Time, Space, and Substance are already informational through and through. Look at the words information theory reaches for when it needs to name where information lives. Channel. Bearer. Register. Substrate. Carrier. Medium. Every one is a word for something. Information is descriptive. It needs something to describe.

Information requires distinction to be information; transition requires succession to be transition; processing requires persistence to be processing. Strip the roles and what remains is not a more fundamental informational substrate but ∅. Wheeler's slogan, on the present account, runs in both directions: it comes from bit only where bit is already the output of T, S, and Φ doing their work. The unreasonable effectiveness of mathematics in describing physical structure (which *it from bit* implicitly trades on) is taken up directly at [§4.3.6](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-6).

*What converges.* Five moves, five concessions. A bit requires difference to be a bit: a difference that makes a difference is already three, distinction (Space), being and medium (Substance), and directed registration (Time). A mathematical structure requires determinate relations among its elements and therefore supports the difference-role. The temporal and bearer roles require an additional realization premise; mathematical consistency or plenitude alone does not supply them. Computation instantiates each role at the level of the computing: temporal evolution, persistent beings, distinct units, with Landauer's principle recording the thermodynamic cost of that instantiation. Ontic structural realism drops the bearer and keeps the pattern, and a pattern is a pattern of something: the node it relocates the bearer into is still a something. The retreat to information-as-substrate names every locale of information in structural vocabulary (channel, bearer, register, medium) and adds a fifth instance of the same concession.

### 4.1.6 Quinean Modal Skepticism {#sec-4-1-6}

Quine's modal skepticism is a thoroughgoing rejection of the modal vocabulary, and the position has not been refuted so much as outlasted by the literatures that find ways to work around it. "Two Dogmas of Empiricism" [-@quine1951] attacks the analytic/synthetic distinction on which much prior modal regimentation depended; "Reference and Modality" [-@quine1953] shows that quantifying into modal contexts produces the notorious failures of substitutivity that *de re* essentialism is supposed to license; *Word and Object* [-@quine1960] turns the screw further with the indeterminacy of translation, on which essential properties cannot be picked out across translation manuals. The proposed cure is austerity: keep the language of regimented science (extensional first-order logic, logic sensitive only to reference and truth-value, not to meaning or modal force, plus the working vocabulary of physics and biology), drop the language of necessity, get on with the work.

@follesdal1986 and @burgess1997 carry the position forward in modal logic; @gibbard1975 develops the contingent-identity wedge that presses against essentialism from within; Williamson's *Modal Logic as Metaphysics* [-@williamson2013, ch. 2] is the contemporary acknowledgment that the position remains the floor any modal account must clear. Where the present argument needs *de re* necessities (that the structural roles obtain in virtue of what they are, not in virtue of how we describe them) Quine's apparatus stands in the way.

The concession runs in full. Quine is right that mid-century modal regimentation imported analyticity as if Carnap had not been answered; right that quantification into modal contexts requires more than its proponents had supplied; right that translation does not pick out essences in any extensionally regimented way. The position closes more loose modal arguments than it opens, and any argument for necessary structural conditions has to clear the Quinean floor before it earns its conclusion. The Quinean tool has tracked something real about how modal vocabulary had been used; the question is whether it tracks something real about the structural conditions [§2.6](the-argument.html#sec-2-6) establishes. Three forms of the Quinean move press the objection at three resolutions.

*First.* The classical analyticity form runs against the present account directly. Necessities, on this reading, are analytic in disguise: "Time is causally structured succession" is a stipulative truth about how we use "Time," not a discovery about what any change-permitting world contains. Modal claims trade on hidden synonymies, and once the synonymies are exposed there is nothing left for necessity to track. Gibbard's [-@gibbard1975] contingent-identity wedge sharpens the pressure: even paradigm *de re* identities can be analyzed as description-relative if essentialism is given up, and the *a posteriori* necessities the Kripkean apparatus delivers (water = H₂O) are recast as terminological decisions about which features fix reference.

The reply runs on the distinction between stipulative definition and structural specification. The role definitions of §[§1.3](groundwork.html#sec-1-3)–1.4 are not synonymy claims about how the English word "Time" relates to the English phrase "causally structured succession"; they are specifications of what any medium hosting transitions must instantiate, derived from what a transition consists in. The derivation does not depend on the term "Time" picking out anything in particular; it shows that succession, distinction, and exchange are the conditions on transition under any vocabulary in which the conditions can be stated. Quine's analyticity critique cuts against synonymy claims dressed up as discoveries; it leaves untouched discoveries that hold in any vocabulary capable of stating them. Gibbard's wedge cuts against essentialism construed as a discovery about which descriptions a thing satisfies; the present account is not in that business. It does not claim that *Time* picks out the same role across worlds; it shows that any world containing transitions instantiates the role, by whatever name.

*Second.* The *de re* / *de dicto* form presses where the first leaves off. Even granting that the structural conditions are not synonymy claims, the Quinean denies that the *de re* reading on which they obtain "of the world rather than of a description" is intelligible at all. Quantifying into modal contexts produces the failures @quine1953 catalogues: "necessarily, 9 is greater than 7" appears true, "9 = the number of planets" is true, "necessarily, the number of planets is greater than 7" is false. The *de re* reading on which a structural condition obtains *of* the medium, independent of how we describe it, is exactly the reading the substitutivity failures rule out. @follesdal1986 and @burgess1997 extend the point: modal logic is a useful instrument for organizing inferences but cannot, on Quinean grounds, be read off as picking out language-independent modal facts.

The reply concedes the substitutivity point and presses where it does not reach. The *de re* readings Quine's catalogue dismisses are readings on which a contingent description ("the number of planets") is treated as if it picked out its referent rigidly across modal contexts. The Kripkean apparatus ([§4.1.1](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-1)) answers the catalogue by distinguishing rigid from non-rigid designators; the present account does not depend on the answer. The structural roles are not picked out by a description that could have picked out something else; they are specified by what a transition requires, and the specification is invariant across the descriptions that satisfy it. There is no Quinean substitutivity failure to find because there is no substitution to perform: any term that satisfies the role-specification of Time picks out the same structural condition, and any term that fails to satisfy it picks out something else. The instrumentalist reading Burgess defends is consistent with this: modal logic is a useful instrument, and the structural conditions are what the instrument has to track to be useful. The instrument's utility on Burgess's own terms is the data the modal account explains.

*Third.* The extensional-regimentation form goes deepest. Even granting that the role-specifications hold in any vocabulary, the Quinean denies that the holding is *modal* in any sense that escapes extensional logic. What looks like necessity is the projectibility of certain predicates within our best science; what looks like *de re* essentialism is the privileged status of certain natural-kind classifications within that science. The work modal vocabulary did before is now done by what regimented science treats as nomological (law-governed, a matter of the laws of nature) and the question whether that treatment tracks something modally robust is exactly what Quine refuses to answer outside the framework. @williamson2013 [ch. 2] presses the contemporary form: the position survives as a methodological stance even where its first-order claims have been answered, and any necessitarian account has to show that the necessities it posits are not artifacts of the science that names them.

The reply distinguishes scope, and it discharges the burden several times over rather than resting on one bridge. The Quinean is right that much of what passed for modal claim at mid-century was projectibility-talk dressed up; right that natural-kind classifications carry methodological privilege within a science without thereby carrying language-independent modal weight; right that the burden is on the necessitarian. What the reply does *not* do is the thing the Quinean would be entitled to reject: assert that projectibility simply *is* structural necessity renamed. Quine has a fully naturalized account of projectibility (entrenched quality-spaces, "Natural Kinds," [-@quine1969b]); answering it by relabeling would beg the question. The conditions [§2.6](the-argument.html#sec-2-6) identifies earn their standing instead by what any nomological practice must presuppose to be one at all, and several independent considerations converge on the same commitment.

*The transcendental consideration.* Actual projection occurs through succession and comparison among distinguishable cases, and Quine's naturalized story invokes persistence and causal selection. This establishes the structure of the actual scientific practice. It does not show that projectibility requires productive law-like causation rather than Humean regularity, or by itself establish the full loaded types in every possible world.

*The indispensability consideration.* Quine's own criterion fixes ontological commitment by what our best science must quantify over ([§2.8.3](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-3)). Any nomological practice quantifies ineliminably over a structured succession of distinguishable, causally interacting items; the structural conditions are not an optional modal overlay but what its bound variables range over. Quinean indispensability can commit the practice to whatever temporal, relational, and physical ontology its best regimentation genuinely quantifies over. Identifying that ontology exactly with the book's T, S, and Φ requires the independent role and realizer arguments; the criterion alone does not supply the identification.

*The invariance consideration.* What keeps the conditions from being artifacts of the science that names them (Williamson's [-@williamson2013, ch. 2] standing worry) is that *every* nomological practice presupposes them, not one. Rival sciences, future regimentations, and Quine's own meta-theory alike must range over them; none can decline them and remain nomological. Projectible predicates vary from science to science; the structural conditions do not, because they are the conditions under which any predicate is projectible at all. This is the thin framework-independence of [§4.1.8](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-8): not a privileged carving beyond all frameworks, but conditions no framework can refuse.

The three considerations support a cumulative reply; none alone converts actual scientific practice into an unrestricted cross-world necessity. The work necessity did before is now done by what our best science treats as nomological, and what any nomological practice operates on, quantifies over, and cannot vary without ceasing to be nomological, is the structural conditions named.

A kindred move drops Quine's program for Williamson's necessitism [-@williamson2013], which keeps the modal vocabulary while denying that contingency is fundamental; that position is engaged at [§4.4.6](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4-6). A different skepticism keeps both the vocabulary and ordinary modal knowledge while denying that the modal faculty is reliable at metaphysical distances [@vanInwagen1998]; because it concedes everything the present section vindicates, it is engaged separately at [§4.1.13](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-13). The adjacent deflationary tradition, modal conventionalism ([§4.1.7](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-7)) and metaontological deflationism ([§4.1.8](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-8)), runs parallel deflations at neighboring resolutions, and the structural reply takes the same form across the family. The regimentation of the structural claims in formal terms that satisfy Quine's extensionalist constraints is carried out at §[§2.10.1](the-argument.html#sec-2-10-1)–2.10.3, showing that the role-specifications are statable without the analytic/synthetic distinction and without quantifying into modal contexts in the way Quine's (1953) catalogue targets; the bound-variable ontology that licenses the existential commitments is laid out specifically at [§2.8.3](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-3).

*What closes.* Three forms of Quinean austerity, and none opens the gap: the classical analyticity form cuts against synonymy dressed up as discovery and leaves structural specifications untouched; the *de re* / *de dicto* form catalogues substitutivity failures for contingent descriptions and leaves role-specifications, which admit no substitution, intact; and the extensional-regimentation form relocates necessity into nomological practice, reinstating the structural conditions as what any such practice operates on. The Quinean refuses the modal vocabulary; the present account shows what the vocabulary picks out, and what it picks out is unaltered by the refusal. However the austerity is run (as analyticity-skepticism, *de re* skepticism, or extensional regimentation) what each form contests is □(T∧S∧Φ) at the *a priori* / constitutive register, supported by the fixed-domain S5 lift from the Cartesian witness together with the separate Structural Requirement and role-to-type premises, the T5/N register line [§4.1.1](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-1) records and [§4.1.2](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-2) makes explicit.

The austerity has done genuine work, as the concession above records. What the austerity has not produced is a configuration of reality in which the structural conditions fail to obtain, and what the catalogue has not produced is a substitution failure that touches role-specification rather than description. The skepticism, taken seriously, narrows to the claim that necessity is an unnecessary word. The argument concedes the possibility and asks what remains when the word is gone. What remains is structure.

### 4.1.7 Modal Conventionalism {#sec-4-1-7}

Alan Sidelle's *Necessity, Essence, and Individuation* [-@sidelle1989] develops the most systematic contemporary defense of the view that necessity is a feature of how we describe the world rather than of the world itself. The argument descends from logical positivism (Ayer's *Language, Truth and Logic* [-@ayer1936] on analyticity, Carnap's "Empiricism, Semantics, and Ontology" [-@carnap1950] on framework-relativity, Quine's [-@quine1951] "Two Dogmas" as the critical pressure the tradition had to absorb) and Sidelle's contribution is to extend the analyticity treatment to *de re* modal claims (necessities about a thing itself rather than about its description). Saying water is necessarily H₂O is, on this picture, a decision about how to use “water” as a natural-kind term rather than a discovery about water.

The position has been pressed in different directions since. Sidelle's "Modality and Objects" [-@sidelle2010] develops the view in response to its critics. Ross Cameron's "On the Source of Necessity" [-@cameron2010] and his subsequent work argue that necessity is grounded in linguistic and conceptual practice without being reducible to it. Amie Thomasson's *Norms and Necessity* [-@thomasson2020] defends an adjacent modal normativism on which modal claims express norms governing concept-use rather than describing language-independent facts. Against the conventionalist tradition, Bob Hale's *Necessary Beings* [-@hale2013] develops the most sustained contemporary critique, and Jonathan Schaffer's necessitarian counter ("Laws for Metaphysical Explanation," [-@schaffer2017]) presses from a different direction.

The argument here does not contest the analyticity of selected modal claims. It contests the claim that all of them are. The structural conditions T, S, and Φ are not stipulated into necessity by linguistic decision; they are the conditions any stipulator must operate within in order to stipulate. (The formal regimentation of these structural claims in terms that satisfy Quine's extensionalist constraints is carried out at §[§2.10.1](the-argument.html#sec-2-10-1)–2.10.3; the bound-variable ontology is at [§2.8.3](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-3).) Any actual proposal and comparison is a structured cognitive and linguistic performance. That secures an act-side point about actual convention-making, not yet the object-side conclusion that every possible world instantiates the full temporal, spatial, and causal types. The global conventionalist still owes an account of the non-conventional resources used to formulate and apply the thesis. Three forms of the conventionalist move sharpen the reply at three resolutions.

*First.* The classical Sidelle [-@sidelle1989] form treats *de re* modal claims as analytic in disguise. “Water is necessarily H₂O” is not a discovery about water; it is a stipulation about how “water” is to be used in modal contexts, with the analyticity hidden by the *de re* surface grammar. The argument generalizes: every necessity is, on examination, a hidden analyticity, and the appearance of language-independent modal fact is the product of unrecognized linguistic decision.

The reply is internal. Stipulations are themselves entities, sequences of marks, sounds, or mental events whose individuation depends on extension, persistence, and contrast with other stipulations. Conventions are configurations within Reality, not grounds prior to it. To say “necessity is conventional” is to use a medium whose conditions are not conventional in any sense the position can recover. Sidelle anticipates the move and replies that the medium itself is conventional all the way down, but the regress closes the position rather than vindicating it. If “medium” is conventional, then the convention that fixes “medium” as conventional is itself a configuration, requiring the very conditions it purports to deflate. Quine's regress presses that conventions cannot alone generate all logical consequence, since applying them requires inferential resources. The structural account may use this against a global conventional reduction, but specifying those resources as the full T, S, and Φ types requires further argument rather than following from the regress itself. Hale's *Necessary Beings* [-@hale2013, ch. 4] presses this point at length: the conventionalist account requires modal vocabulary to state, and the modal vocabulary it requires is not stateable in the conventionalist's preferred terms.

*Second.* Cameron's [-@cameron2010] refinement concedes the medium's structural conditions and presses the thesis at a higher level. Necessity is grounded in linguistic and conceptual practice in the sense that what makes modal claims true is the practice of using modal vocabulary in the way we use it, not in the sense that modal claims are reducible to claims about the practice. The grounding relation is asymmetric: modal facts hold in virtue of practices, but modal facts are not identical to facts about practices. The position survives the regress because it does not deny that practices have structural conditions; it grounds modality in practices and is silent on the structural conditions of practices.

The concession is real. The reply is that Cameron's position succeeds at the cost of being indistinguishable from the present account at the level where the present argument's claim applies. A concrete discursive practice ordinarily involves continuing practitioners, distinguishable acts, and temporal ordering. Those are conditions on such practices; calling them unrestricted modal conditions, and identifying them with the full loaded types, depends on the book's separate structural derivation. The grounding Cameron offers (modality grounded in practice) terminates at conditions on practice that are themselves necessary in every world in which practice exists. The present account names those conditions; Cameron's account leaves them implicit. The remaining disagreement is about whether the structural conditions are best described as conditions on linguistic practice in particular (Cameron) or on any configuration capable of hosting practice or anything else (the present argument).

*Third.* Thomasson's [-@thomasson2020] modal normativism is a refined version. Modal claims do not describe modal facts; they express norms governing concept-use. “Water is necessarily H₂O” does not say anything about water; it endorses a norm about how the concept *water* is to be applied across counterfactual cases. The position is genuinely deflationary about modal facts without being committed to the regress-prone claim that modal claims are reducible to claims about language.

The reply tracks Thomasson's own framework. Actual norm-governed practices distinguish applications and often maintain standards across time. An abstract norm need not itself persist as a physical bearer or be applied in temporal sequence, so the practice-side structure should not be transferred automatically to the norm as an abstract object. Thomasson's normativism does not deny these conditions; it is silent on them, treating them as background to the normative analysis rather than as the locus of modal commitment. The present account makes them explicit. The conditions of a norm's being in force (proposed, applied, maintained in a practice) are what the structural roles secure, and any normativist account that disowns those conditions disowns the apparatus the account requires.

A kindred move presses from outside conventionalism entirely. Schaffer's [-@schaffer2017] necessitarianism argues that the laws governing metaphysical explanation are themselves necessary, but the necessity is not conventional: it is grounded in the structure of explanation itself. The present account agrees with Schaffer that the necessity is not conventional, and adds a constructive specification of what the necessity is grounded in: the structural conditions any configuration capable of being something must instantiate. Where Schaffer leaves the grounding at "the structure of explanation," the present account specifies the structure.

Two adjacent positions live elsewhere. Carnapian framework-deflationism is engaged at [§4.1.8](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-8) (Metaontological Deflationism). Modal fictionalism, which deflates modal commitment by relocating it to a fiction rather than to convention, is engaged at [§4.4.4](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4-4).

*What converges.* The conventionalist tradition has refined itself across thirty-seven years, from Sidelle's classical analyticity-extension (unstable on its own articulation, since stipulations have structural conditions it cannot recover) through Cameron's grounding-asymmetry (consistent with the structural account at the level of conditions on practice) to Thomasson's normativism (consistent at the level of conditions on norms). However the conventionalism is pitched (as analyticity-extension, grounding-asymmetry, or normativism) each form locates the source of □(T∧S∧Φ) in a derivative register (convention, practice, norm), while the register at which the modality holds is *a priori* / constitutive, supported by the fixed-domain S5 lift from the Cartesian witness together with the independent Structural Requirement and role-to-type premises, the T5/N register line [§4.1.1](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-1) records and [§4.1.2](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-2) makes explicit.

Sidelle's 1989 book was written when the analyticity treatment of modality looked, after Quine's "Two Dogmas," like a project that had not survived the mid-century. The intervening decades have been a long argument that selected analyticities can be defended even if Quine's general critique stands. The argument has succeeded in part: there are conventional necessities, and the analyticity of selected modal claims is a stable position. What the long argument has not produced is a global conventionalism that survives examination of its own articulation. The conditions for the convention are not conventional. The structural roles are what any convention presupposes.

### 4.1.8 Metaontological Deflationism {#sec-4-1-8}

A family of contemporary metaontological positions argues that disputes in fundamental ontology are verbal rather than substantive. Different ontological vocabularies are different languages, equally adequate to the world; the choice between them is pragmatic, not factual.

The lineage runs from Rudolf Carnap's "Empiricism, Semantics, and Ontology" [-@carnap1950] (distinguishing internal questions answerable within a linguistic framework from external questions of pragmatic framework-choice) through Eli Hirsch's quantifier variance (the view that different ontological frameworks have different quantifier-meanings, each equally adequate to reality; *Quantifier Variance and Realism* [-@hirsch2011], collecting work from 2002 onward) to Amie Thomasson's easy ontology (*Ontology Made Easy* [-@thomasson2015]). David Chalmers's "Ontological Anti-Realism" (in *Metametaphysics: New Essays on the Foundations of Ontology*, ed. Chalmers, Manley and Wasserman [-@chalmers2009]) develops a more refined version on which there is no fact of the matter about absolute existence, while internal-to-framework existence is unproblematic. Matti Eklund's "The Picture of Reality as an Amorphous Lump" (in Sider, Hawthorne and Zimmerman's *Contemporary Debates in Metaphysics*) defends a related but distinct position on which different carving-schemes are equivalent descriptions of a structurally underdetermined reality. On this picture, asking whether T, S, and Φ are necessary is asking the wrong kind of question; there is no language-independent fact of the matter for an answer to track.

The deflationist's neutrality is not neutral. Different ontological vocabularies must be vocabularies *of something*: different ways of carving up a shared reality. If there were no common reality, there would be nothing for distinct vocabularies to be alternative descriptions of. The deflationist's framework presupposes that this reality has whatever conditions are required for distinct descriptions to be applied to the same thing: extension over which carvings can vary, persistence for the same matter to be re-described, distinction between description and described. These are the structural conditions under different names. ("Configuration" throughout this reply names whatever jointly instantiates the three structural roles T, S, and Φ as derived at [§2.6](the-argument.html#sec-2-6); it is shorthand for that joint-instantiation condition rather than an additional ontological category. The formal regimentation of the structural claims in terms that satisfy Quine's extensionalist constraints is carried out at §[§2.10.1](the-argument.html#sec-2-10-1)–2.10.3.) Three forms of the deflationary move sharpen what each version commits to.

*First.* The Carnapian framework form treats ontological questions as internal to a chosen linguistic framework. “Are there numbers?” is well-formed inside the framework of arithmetic and answerable trivially in the affirmative; outside the framework it is a pragmatic question about whether to adopt the framework. Hirsch's quantifier variance generalizes the move: different frameworks have different quantifier-meanings, each equally adequate to reality. There is no privileged sense of “exists” against which framework-choice can be assessed.

The reply is internal to the position's own apparatus. For two frameworks to be alternative carvings of a shared reality, the shared reality must have whatever properties license distinct alternative carvings: at minimum, sufficient extension to be carved differently (S), persistence across the alternative carvings (Φ), and the temporal ordering of carving-events that lets one framework be adopted, then another, then evaluated comparatively (T). Hirsch concedes that frameworks must be alternatives of something but holds that what they are alternatives of can be specified only within some framework. The concession is enough. If the something has whatever properties are required to be the something the frameworks are alternatives of, those properties are the structural conditions, and they obtain whether or not any framework names them.

This is the thin claim, not the heavyweight one: not that some framework-transcendent carving is metaphysically privileged, but that whatever a framework must quantify over in order to be a framework at all already instantiates the roles. On Quine's bound-variable criterion ([§2.8.3](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-3); with the later formal discussion at [§2.10.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-10-2)), the commitment is read off what any framework-comparison must range over; the conditions are framework-independent in the sense that no framework can decline them, not in the sense of a privileged carving lying behind every framework and reachable from none.

That the roles are Reality's and not the framework's is earned below, on the deflationist's own criterion, once the deepest form of the position is in view. Carnap's "external questions" are pragmatic only on the assumption that there is no fact of the matter outside the framework. The assumption is the position's central claim, and the assumption is what the present argument contests. It is a contest whose founding form is Quine's, who rejects any principled internal/external distinction in "On Carnap's Views on Ontology" [-@quine1951b] on the strength of the ontological-commitment criterion of "On What There Is" [-@quine1948]. What the present account adds to that Quinean realism is the specification of the conditions a substrate must satisfy to be the something rival frameworks are alternatives of.

*Second.* Thomasson's [-@thomasson2015] easy ontology is the most carefully developed contemporary version. Existence questions are answerable trivially given conceptual competence: “Are there tables?” follows from “There are particles arranged tablewise” plus the application conditions of “table”; “Are there numbers?” follows from “There are five apples” plus the application conditions of “number”. The position is deflationary about ontology while remaining committed to the trivial truth of ordinary existence claims. There are no hard ontological questions because the apparent hardness reflects only confusion about application conditions.

The reply tracks Thomasson's own framework. Application conditions are themselves features that must be specified: a concept's application conditions persist across applications (Φ), distinguish cases of application from cases of non-application (S), and operate across the temporal succession of applications (T). Thomasson's account is consistent with the present account at the level where the present account's claim applies: the application conditions are themselves features of a configured reality, and the conditions of their being application conditions are the structural roles. Thomasson's deflationism succeeds at deflating ontology in the sense she means; it does not deflate the conditions on which the deflationary apparatus operates. The remaining disagreement is whether the structural conditions are themselves substantive ontological commitments (the present view) or further easy commitments derivable from concept-use (a possible Thomassonian reply). The present argument takes the Triconditional machinery of [§2.6](the-argument.html#sec-2-6) (especially the Mutual Containment Result at [§2.6.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-5)) as the case for the first reading: the structural roles mutually require one another and cannot be derived from any prior conceptual base.

*Third.* The Chalmers [-@chalmers2009] and Eklund [-@eklund2008] positions occupy philosophically refined ground. Chalmers's ontological anti-realism distinguishes lightweight quantifiers (used in ordinary discourse, indifferent to deep ontological commitment) from heavyweight quantifiers (used in fundamental ontology, subject to framework-relativity). The position holds that heavyweight ontological questions have no determinate answer while lightweight ones have trivial answers. Eklund's position treats reality as a structurally underdetermined "amorphous lump" that admits of multiple equivalent carvings, with no carving privileged over others. Both positions sharpen the deflationary tradition by making it consistent with the trivial truth of ordinary existence claims.

The reply concedes the lightweight/heavyweight distinction and presses where the heavyweight claim sits. Chalmers's position requires that there be lightweight-but-real configurations (otherwise lightweight existence claims would not be trivially true) and that no heavyweight fact about absolute existence obtains. The present account's claim is not a heavyweight claim about a privileged absolute carving; it is a claim about what any configuration capable of being something (at any weight) must instantiate. If Chalmers's lightweight configurations include extension, persistence, and temporal succession (and they must, on pain of being indistinguishable from no configuration at all), then the structural conditions obtain at the lightweight level Chalmers grants. Eklund's amorphous lump faces the same pressure. The more charitable reading of the position is that the lump is *underdetermined by privileged carvings* rather than structureless: reality admits multiple equivalent carving-schemes, none of which is the metaphysically privileged one. The reply does not require treating the lump as structureless. Even reality underdetermined-by-privileged-carvings must still support three things. It must support the framework-comparison the position invokes (different carvings must be distinguishable from one another and from the lump they carve). It must support the application of each carving to the lump (each scheme must operate on something that persists as what it operates on). And it must support the temporal succession of carving-acts by which one scheme is adopted, evaluated, and replaced by another. Those three are the structural conditions under different names, and they obtain at whichever level reality is configured to admit alternative carvings at all. The ∅ fork then sharpens what the position itself commits to: a lump structureless enough to admit any carving whatever is a lump indistinguishable from ∅ ([§2.7](the-argument.html#sec-2-7)); a lump with sufficient structure to admit some carvings but not others is a lump with the structural conditions named.

The position can be sharpened across all three forms into the claim that every ontological commitment is internal to a framework. The sharpening is unstable. The claim itself is either internal to a framework (in which case it is one ontological commitment among others, not the metalevel verdict it presents itself as) or external, in which case it asserts a framework-independent fact about the relation between frameworks and the world, contradicting its own deflationism. There is no third position from which the verdict can be issued without using the apparatus the verdict denies. Thomasson's reply [-@thomasson2015, ch. 3] (that the metaontological claim is itself trivially true given the application conditions of metaontological vocabulary) relocates the instability rather than dissolving it: the application conditions of metaontological vocabulary are themselves features of a configured reality, and the conditions of their being application conditions are what the present argument names.

*The retreat to the framework.* One reply remains. Grant everything so far: that no framework can decline the three roles, that every carving and every comparison of carvings already deploys succession, distinction, and exchange. The deflationist can still say this fixes only a fact about frameworks (about what any scheme must presuppose to be a scheme) and not a fact about Reality. That the roles are presupposed by all our descriptions is one thing; that they are Reality's own structure, owing nothing to the describing, is another, and the transcendental result delivers only the first. The line is Stroud's: that we cannot think past a structure shows how we must think, not how things stand.

The retreat has no ground to stand on, and the reason is internal to the position once more. The deflationary apparatus rests on a single criterion of what it is for something to be objective rather than framework-relative: to be objective is to be invariant under the choice of framework, and to be merely framework-relative is to vary with it.

Quantifier variance is the thesis that what exists varies with the quantifier-meaning a framework supplies; the lightweight/heavyweight distinction is the distinction between what holds inside a chosen scheme and what would hold across all of them; the verdict that no carving is privileged just is the claim that every candidate joint varies across admissible frameworks. Strip the position of the invariance-criterion and it cannot state its own thesis: "privileged" means framework-transcendent, and framework-transcendence is measured as invariance. The criterion is not optional equipment; it is what gives the deflationary verdict its content.

Apply it. The three roles do not vary across frameworks; they are what every framework presupposes, the fixed point under the operation *adopt a different scheme*. Framework-invariance supplies evidence that the roles are not artifacts of any one scheme. It does not, without a further bridge, entail that they are mind-independent features of Reality; a deflationist may treat them as constraints on every admissible framework. The dispute therefore narrows to whether invariance is merely transcendental or genuinely ontological. The present account argues for the latter, but it should not present that bridge as forced by deflationism alone. The transcendental fact, read through the criterion the deflationist must hold in order to speak at all, counts as transcendent by the deflationist's own measure.

This is the heavyweight claim in the only sense the opening allows it. *Reality* is fixed at [§1.1](groundwork.html#sec-1-1) as a structural-role term (what any content presupposes, its reference set by what the role requires and not by which thing fills it). The constitutive language there names the structural shape of the primitive modal field, not an essence prior to it. The present conclusion claims exactly that and no more: the roles belong to Reality in that they are invariant across every scheme in which anything is configured at all, not in the sense of an essence lying behind all configuration and reachable from none.

The deflationist who demands the second sense before conceding the first asks for a target [§1.1](groundwork.html#sec-1-1) already declines to posit. The demand purchases nothing: a structure that does no work in any framework and is reachable from none is, by the ∅ fork, indistinguishable from the absence of structure ([§2.7](the-argument.html#sec-2-7)). What [§1.1.1](groundwork.html#sec-1-1-1) leaves conditional is supported here but not discharged by invariance alone: what is invariant across languages is internal to no single language, yet may still be characterized by a deflationist as a universal condition on representation rather than as mind-independent ontology.

One regress is owed an answer. The deflationist can lift the retreat a level: the claim that the roles are invariant across all frameworks is itself advanced within a framework (a meta-framework that individuates schemes and ranges over them) so what is shown is invariance within that meta-framework, not invariance as such. But the trilemma is indifferent to level. The meta-claim that one has shown only invariance-within-M is itself either internal to some further scheme, in which case it varies across schemes and is, by the criterion, non-objective, and so cannot deliver the objective verdict it pronounces; or it is external, a framework-transcendent fact about the relation between meta-frameworks and the roles, which is the thing the position forbids itself.

Nor does the regress escape the roles by climbing: any meta-framework that individuates frameworks and ranges over them is itself carving. It requires distinction to hold its frameworks apart, exchange to compare them, succession to adopt one and then another. Each ascent instantiates the roles it is meant to rise above. The invariance is therefore not invariance at a level but invariance the hierarchy cannot exit; the regress, far from undercutting the result, is its demonstration.

A kindred move worth marking. Modal conventionalism ([§4.1.7](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-7)) runs a parallel deflationary argument at the level of modal claims rather than existence claims; the structural reply takes the same form. Modal fictionalism ([§4.4.4](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4-4)) deflates modal commitment by relocating it to a fiction; again the structural conditions return at the level of the storytelling. The deflationary family across these three sections shares a common structure and a common vulnerability: each version succeeds at deflating its target only by leaving the conditions on its deflationary apparatus implicit, and each, on examination, presupposes the structural roles at the level its deflation operates.

*What converges.* Three forms of metaontological deflationism (Carnapian framework-relativity, Thomassonian easy ontology, Chalmers–Eklund refined deflationism), and each, fully developed, is consistent with the present account at the level its claim applies: the Carnapian form requires a substrate frameworks are alternatives of, Thomasson's form requires application conditions, and the Chalmers–Eklund form requires lightweight-but-real configurations or a structurally non-trivial lump. Each of these already has the structural conditions. However the deflationism is pitched, each form denies □(T∧S∧Φ) a framework-transcendent register, and each is answered at the same fixed point: the register is *a priori* / constitutive, the register line fixed at [§4.1.1](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-1)–[§4.1.2](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-2).

The deflationist who presses anyway operates within the structural conditions while declaring them undecidable. The declaration is a configuration within Reality, and so is the framework that hosts it. Both fall within the scope of the argument they contest.

### 4.1.9 Wittgensteinian Quietism {#sec-4-1-9}

Wittgensteinian quietism comes in distinct varieties that share a common stance: philosophical theses, including metaphysical theses about the structural ground of reality, are not properly to be argued for or against but to be diagnosed. The varieties differ in what diagnosis amounts to.

The Tractarian Wittgenstein [-@wittgenstein1921], and the resolute reading developed by @diamond1991 and @conant2002 on which the *Tractatus*'s philosophical sentences are themselves nonsense to be climbed and discarded, holds that metaphysical sentences fail to express propositions. They are not false; they lack truth-conditions. The proper response is silence: to climb the ladder of philosophical analysis and then throw it away.

The later, *Investigations*-derived varieties operate differently. Hacker [with Baker, -@bakerHacker1980; -@bakerHacker1985; Hacker, -@hacker2001] defends the orthodox Wittgensteinian view that metaphysical claims are grammatical confusions: when we ask whether time is real, we have misread the grammar of *real* and projected an answerable question where none lives. @mcdowell1994 develops a therapeutic quietism in epistemology and philosophy of mind: philosophy's task is not to construct theories but to dissolve the appearance of problems by clarifying the conceptual framework that generated them. @cavell1979 goes further: skepticism cannot be refuted by argument but only acknowledged, and the criteria for our concepts come from forms of life rather than from any standpoint outside them. On all three readings, a sustained metaphysical argument like the present one is not engaging a question the quietist takes to be live; it is exhibiting a confusion the quietist takes its task to clarify.

The challenge is sharper than ordinary skepticism. The quietist does not argue that the present argument is wrong. The quietist argues that it is not the kind of thing that can be wrong, because it is not the kind of thing that can be right.

The reply has three parts, addressing the varieties in turn.

*First.* The Tractarian framework distinguishes saying from showing: certain features of the world cannot be stated within language but can be exhibited by what language does. Time, Space, and Substance, on the present argument, are precisely such features. Every act of language exhibits them, 'exhibits' here in the sense fixed by the ∅-fork at [§2.7](the-argument.html#sec-2-7): any act that is not ∅ instantiates the structural conditions, their joint instantiation being what counts as there being an act at all. The argument is not the proposition *T, S, and Φ are necessary*; the argument is the structural exhibition of what utterance, distinction, and persistence require. A Tractarian who grants showing has granted what the argument needs; the resolute reader, who discards showing along with the rest of the ladder, is met not here but by the performative point below, since the climbing and discarding are themselves enacted.

*Second.* The Hacker–Baker line says metaphysical questions are misuses of language; McDowell says they are appearances generated by a conceptual framework whose clarification dissolves them. Both readings require a coherent distinction between misuse and use, or between confused appearance and clarified perception. Drawing the distinction is itself an activity. It occurs over time, differentiates one form of words from another, and persists through the diagnostician. The diagnostic activity exhibits T, S, and Φ no less than any first-order metaphysical claim does. The therapy does not undo what makes the therapy possible.

*Third.* Cavell's deepest move is that philosophical claims rest on criteria that come from forms of life, and that a form of life is not a thesis but a way of being-in-language. The present argument does not contest this. It identifies what any form of life (any way of using criteria, any practice of acknowledgment) requires. The structural conditions are not criteria offered from a standpoint outside the form of life. They are what occupying any form of life involves. Cavell's acknowledgment of skepticism is itself a sustained activity; the activity has the structure the argument identifies; the acknowledgment does not float free of what makes acknowledgment possible.

*The grammatical reading, owned.* The quietist presses one step further: if the only thing that would count against 'every act exhibits T, S, and Φ' is ∅ (the absence of any act at all) then the claim has no contrastive use among actual cases, and a claim with no contrastive use is grammatical rather than substantive. The response is not to resist this but to accept it, on one condition. The claim is indeed constitutive: it does not report a feature some acts have and others lack; it states what *counts* as there being an act at all. But this concedes nothing to quietism, whose charge is that metaphysical claims are *confusions*, pseudo-questions to be dissolved. A constitutive truth whose only alternative is ∅ is the opposite of a confusion. The grammar is not idle. It marks the one boundary that does not fall between cases but between there being cases and there being nothing at all: the line between something and ∅. To call that “merely grammatical” is to mistake the floor of the world for a turn of phrase. The claim earns a constitutive register precisely because its proposed countercase is absolute structural absence rather than another ordinary act. Still, the exhibition of the roles in actual speech or diagnosis establishes an act-side result. The cross-world □(T∧S∧Φ) conclusion depends on the modal and role-to-type arguments developed elsewhere; quietist performance alone does not supply it.

*What converges.* The dialectical point extends across all the varieties considered here. Where refusing to articulate an objection is itself a performed act of declination, it involves persistence, distinction, and an ordered episode. Mere absence of speech, however, is not automatically such an act and does not by itself instantiate the full triad. The performative point applies to enacted quietism, not to silence considered simply as no tokened response. Quietism, enacted, is the position that exhibits structure most economically.

### 4.1.10 The Source of Possibility {#sec-4-1-10}

The PSR demand is met at [§4.1.3](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-3) by showing that Nature is not a thing that grounds itself but what grounding consists in. A residual question remains: can an entity **within the modal domain** be explanatorily prior to real possibility, conferring content on the global range W that ◇ quantifies over? The answer runs by disjunctive elimination on the candidate's own modal status. It is deliberately narrower than the claim that every possible essence-prior or primitive grounding account has been refuted by contradiction.

The position pressed against is the family of grounding accounts that take possibility as a derivative phenomenon: neo-Fregean abstractionism on modal grounds [@hale2013], Lewisian reduction of modality to concrete possible worlds [@lewis1986], Williamsonian necessitism [@williamson2013], dispositionalist grounding of possibility in the potentialities of actual objects [@vetter2015], engaged on its own terms at [§4.1.12](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-12), and the theistic moves that locate modality in a divine intellect or divine nature [@adams1983; @pruss2011; @leftow2012]; the last of these, pressed as an argument from modality's need of a ground to God's existence, is engaged on its own terms at [§5.1.8](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-1-8), whereas the result established here runs purely at the level of any candidate's modal status.

*Definition.* Let *source of possibility* name any X such that ◇p (for some non-empty range of p) holds in virtue of X. The "in virtue of" relation is left maximally general: causal, metaphysical, conceptual, intellectual, or explanatory grounding all qualify. The argument does not turn on which grounding relation is in view.

::: {.premise}
**Modal Exclusivity** · *Premises*

1. If X is a source of possibility, then ◇p holds in virtue of X (Definition).

1. Every candidate X has exactly one modal status: ¬◇X (impossible: true in no world), ◇X ∧ ¬□X (contingent: true in at least one world but not in every world), or □X (necessary: true in every world). The three cases are mutually exclusive and jointly exhaustive.

:::

*The impossible case.* ¬◇X. If X is impossible, X has no instances and no relata. Nothing is the case in virtue of what is not the case. The impossible is not a source but the absence of one.

*The contingent case.* ◇X ∧ ¬□X. If X is possible without being necessary, ◇X is itself a fact within the modal field. The proposed source of ◇ presupposes ◇ in the specification of its own modal status. The field is not grounded by one of its own features.

*The necessary case.* □X. This horn must be met in its strongest form, the one that grants the most. That X is necessary does not by itself bar it from being explanatorily prior: grounding priority and modal status are distinct, and an item may be necessary without being explanatorily inert — essence need not reduce to any modal fact [@fine1994], and the necessitist may hold X necessary yet grounding [@williamson2013]. Concede the orthogonality and the modal classification alone does not close the case. Describing X as necessary uses □, but it does not follow that X's nature or grounding activity is ontologically posterior to the modal field; a Finean essentialist may hold that □X is true because of X's essence. What the classification shows is narrower: the modal description □X cannot itself explain the content of ◇ without circularity. Excluding X as an essence-prior source requires an additional theory of grounding, not the modal trilemma alone. The point is not that necessity precludes priority, but that priority *to ◇* is unavailable to anything whose own status is already modal.

**Modal Exclusivity, scoped.** *No candidate's modal status by itself explains the modal domain: impossible and contingent candidates fail as global sources, while a necessary candidate requires an additional, non-modal account of how its essence or grounding activity confers modal content. The trilemma exposes a circularity burden; it does not refute every essence-prior source by modal classification alone.*

*The self-grounding rejoinder.* A defender may concede the trilemma and posit that possibility grounds itself, that ◇ is its own ground. Two readings exhaust the move. On the deflationary reading, "self-grounding" is a notational variant of primitivism: ◇ is not derived from anything more basic, and the Principle stands. On the substantive reading, grounding is a reflexive relation on ◇, and the field grounds itself. Here the analytic literature on ground divides the relation in two [@fine2012]. *Strict* ground is irreflexive: nothing strictly grounds itself [@schaffer2009; @fine2012]. So if the rejoinder means that ◇ strictly grounds ◇, irreflexivity rules it out directly. *Weak* ground is reflexive by construction (every fact weakly grounds itself) so ◇ does weakly ground ◇; but weak self-grounding is just the absence of any strict ground, which is primitivism stated in the grounding idiom rather than an alternative to it. Either way ◇ has no strict source. This is also what accommodates the minority dissent that admits reflexive or non-well-founded grounding [@jenkins2011]: that dissent is a thesis about weak ground and the failure of well-foundedness, not a denial of strict-ground irreflexivity, so it is absorbed by the fork rather than set aside as a bare commitment. The substantive reading does not escape the trilemma; it renames its floor.

*The classical-theism rejoinder.* Aquinas-style classical theism does not propose God as a source of possibility distinct from God; on divine simplicity, God *is* the modal field (*ipsum esse subsistens* applied to modality). The move sidesteps the trilemma by collapsing the source/sourced distinction. The collapse delivers one of two results. On the relabeling reading, *God* renames "the primitive modal field," in which case the Principle stands and the relabeling is theological vocabulary rather than a modal-foundations counterexample. On the predicate-bearing reading, the modal field carries predicates classical theism attributes to God (will, intellect, agency), which is the engagement [§5.2](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-2) and [§5.1](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-1) take up, not a counterexample to the present Principle.

*The transcendence rejoinder.* A defender may place X beyond modality altogether: neither possible, necessary, nor impossible. That proposal is not refuted merely by repeating the trilemma, because the trilemma classifies candidates whose modal status is already in view. The present result instead marks a burden. If X is said to explain W, the account must explain how an entity outside real possibility bears an explanatory relation to the domain of real possibilities without thereby being specified as one more item in that relation. A classical-theist or Finean essentialist may regard that relation as primitive or essence-prior. The chapter does not close that option by contradiction. It shows that it is no longer a modal-semantic explanation of possibility: it is an additional metaphysical posit whose credentials must be argued in its own theory of grounding. The theological version is engaged at [§5.1.8](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-1-8); the essence-priority question remains the live gloss identified below.

The same closure bears on the question [§2.6.1](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-1) and [§3.5.3](convergence.html#sec-3-5-3) defer to this section: whether the realizer biconditionals, □(T↔(S∧Φ)) and □(Φ↔(T∧S)), state a structural-functional necessity or a Finean real definition under another name. The two readings must be prised apart from what depends on them. The *type-upgrades* of [§3.5.3](convergence.html#sec-3-5-3) need only that the biconditionals are necessary, and they are necessary on either reading — a real definition is necessary if anything is — so □(T↔(S∧Φ)) transmits its necessity to the spatial and persistence types under modus ponens whichever reading is correct. The type-layer therefore closes even for a reader who keeps the Finean essence-prior gloss; nothing in the structural conclusion is hostage to the outcome.

What the elimination above underwrites is the *further* claim the modal-monist commitment ([§2.8.6](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-6)) makes: that this necessity is not seated in the essence of an item standing prior to the modal field. That claim is not secured by declaring every standing a modal standing — the Finean is entitled to hold that essence, were it prior, would ground modal facts rather than stand among them. The 'occupying a role is itself a possibility' reply used against a *source of ◇* above does not carry over here: there the role at issue was the sourcing of ◇ itself, so standing in it was intra-modal by construction, whereas a realizer biconditional makes no claim to source ◇, and importing the move would beg the question. It is secured only to the extent the trilemma applies: any candidate put forward as the essence-bearing ground has its own modal status (□X, ◇X, or ¬◇X) and is to that extent specified from within the field rather than before it, leaving the essence-prior reading with no definiendum the elimination has not already located inside ◇.

A committed essentialist can decline that last step; if so, the disagreement is over the gloss on a necessity both sides grant, not over the necessity the biconditionals transmit. The structural-functional reading is the one this account adopts and the one the modal monism of [§2.8.6](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-6) requires: the biconditionals record what any medium hosting succession must be, the structural feature reality *is* rather than an essence some entity *has*.

Nor does the presupposition improve on iteration. Let the defender universalize: every possibility is sourced. Then the sourcing (itself a modal fact) is a further possibility, and by the defender's own thesis it requires a source; so, in turn, does the possibility of that. The chain forks. Either some link goes un-sourced, which concedes the Principle outright, or none does, and the sourcing relation never steps outside the field it was meant to ground. The regress is vicious not because it fails to terminate but because no stage of it is ever prior to ◇; the explanatory debt the account incurred is never discharged. Its one exit (that ◇ grounds its own possibility, closing the chain in a loop) is already foreclosed: a strict-grounding loop is barred by the irreflexivity of strict ground, and a weak self-grounding loop collapses into primitivism, as the self-grounding rejoinder established. What stands is a dilemma whose floor is the one-step presupposition: primitivism, or a regress that never leaves the field, with self-grounding shut.

The exotic placement of X buys no exemption from this. The via negativa is addressed at [§5.2.2](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-2-2), on its own register. The Principle holds at the relation level against any candidate placeable at any level.

*What is established.* No candidate whose own status is stated in modal terms can be a thing-style source of the modal domain it already inhabits. The impossible and contingent horns fail directly; the necessary horn remains inside the domain whose source it was meant to supply. The result blocks internal modal grounds — divine intellect, concrete worlds, abstractions, or necessary entities specified as modal occupants. It does not settle whether a committed essentialist or transcendence theorist can posit an essence-prior ground; that is a further metaphysical cost and a live dispute, not a contradiction the present trilemma alone supplies. The Necessity of Nature identifies the structural content of the global domain; Modal Exclusivity establishes that no modal item within it confers that domain from outside. Its lateral counterpart, Modal Closure ([§2.8.4](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-4)), records that no unnecessary alternative stands alongside it from outside.

*The impossibility pole.* The same elimination runs on any candidate source of impossibility. Let a *source of impossibility* be any X such that ¬◇p holds in virtue of X; the trilemma on X's own modal status is unchanged. An impossible X has no relata in virtue of which anything could hold. A contingent X is itself a fact within the field and presupposes the modality it would confer. A necessary X cannot explain impossibility merely by being described with □; whether its essence can ground modal exclusion remains the same live grounding question as on the possibility side. Modal Exclusivity is therefore bilateral only as a diagnostic: modal status alone does not source either ◇ or ¬◇. The stronger claim that both poles are primitive requires the structural-functional account adopted here, not the trilemma by itself. The field is sourceless at both poles. This closes the residual voluntarist retreat that grants possibility its primitiveness but relocates the necessary truths, or the standing of the impossible, in a divine intellect or will (the created-truths tradition; theistic activism on the necessary truths, @leftow2012); that inference is met on its own terms at [§5.1.8](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-1-8), while the result here holds at the level of any candidate's modal status. What Way–Possibility Convertibility ([§3.2.5](convergence.html#sec-3-2-5)) records on the possible side has its dual on the impossible side: to be impossible is for there to be no way to be, and the absence of a way is not conferred by an antecedent ground but is, like its positive twin, a structural feature reality is rather than has.

### 4.1.11 Pizzi's Impossibility of Nothingness {#sec-4-1-11}

David Pizzi's *The Impossibility of Nothingness: A Foundational Argument for Necessary Existence*[@pizzi2025] is the closest contemporary cousin of the impossibility-driven recovery this argument runs across the lines of [§3.2](convergence.html#sec-3-2)–[§3.3](convergence.html#sec-3-3) and the convergence tallied at [§3.5](convergence.html#sec-3-5), and at [§5.1.1](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-1-1). The dialectical situation is symmetric and instructive: Pizzi and the present account converge on the same modal floor (that absolute nothingness is impossible and that something must exist necessarily) by closely related performative and self-refutational machinery. They diverge on what sits at that floor. Pizzi concludes that something exists necessarily (□∃x x) and explicitly declines to arbitrate among the candidates that could occupy the necessary slot. The present account concludes that the structural Triconditions T ∧ S ∧ Φ exist necessarily (□(T ∧ S ∧ Φ)) and arbitrates among the candidates Pizzi leaves open. The same final move (closing modal space against ∅) yields a bare-existential conclusion in Pizzi and a determinate-content conclusion here.

Pizzi's argument runs three reductios against the metaphysical possibility of total absence and bridges them through a single theorem. The first reductio targets the truth-maker logic of *nothing exists*: given truthmaker maximalism, if that proposition were possibly true it would need a truth-maker; the proposed absence cannot stand in the truth-making relation without being something. The result therefore depends on the truthmaker requirement rather than following from the proposition alone. Quantification over absences therefore collapses. The second reductio targets representations of the proposition: actual assertion and formal modeling presuppose syntactic and semantic resources. That is a strong act-side or model-side result, though an opponent may deny that resources used to represent a scenario must exist inside the represented scenario. The third reductio targets empty-domain semantics. Whether actuality operators force non-emptiness depends on the quantified modal semantics adopted, so this line constrains particular formalisms rather than settling every empty-world model by definition. The bridging theorem assembles the three: since each path forecloses the possibility that nothing exists, by the modal duality ¬◇¬X ≡ □X it follows that something exists necessarily. The argument runs at the same logical strength as the convergence of lines catalogued at [§3.2](convergence.html#sec-3-2)–[§3.3](convergence.html#sec-3-3) and tallied at [§3.5](convergence.html#sec-3-5): classical modal duality, no S5, no positive theology, no conceivability premise outside the structural-self-defeat asymmetry the conceivability-inversion line develops at [§3.3.4](convergence.html#sec-3-3-4).

A note on formalization for the Pizzi-mode reader. Pizzi's three reductios run in formal modal-logical mode and converge on □∃x x via classical modal duality. That result is significant but deliberately thin: it establishes necessary existence without identifying the necessary content.

The present argument reaches □(T∧S∧Φ) by a different line. It needs the fixed-domain modal theorem, the Cartesian witness of change, and the Structural Requirement that any change-permitting world realizes the Conditions. The move from □∃x x to □◇C is not licensed by modal duality alone, and the present account should not attribute such a T-completeness lemma to Pizzi's result. A nonempty world might contain abstract or otherwise thin content without thereby realizing genuine change. The structural conclusion therefore requires the independent role- and type-level arguments Chapters 2–3 develop.

The boundary is worth marking in the object language as well. The □ in □(T∧S∧Φ) ranges over worlds, while T is a within-world structural condition, so the box governs whether the Triconditions obtain at each world, not any temporal ordering internal to one of them.

The methodological convergence is close enough to require an account of what the present argument does that Pizzi does not. Two answers. First, Pizzi's three paths each target the assertion or modeling of ∅: what happens when one tries to *state* or *represent* the empty case. The negation line of [§3.3.2](convergence.html#sec-3-3-2) closes a parallel gap by targeting the *operation* that would produce ∅ from a populated case: stripping structure away. This line is not among Pizzi's three; he does not run an introduction-by-subtraction argument, since his framework treats ∅ as a candidate state whose semantics must be evaluated, not as a state that would have to be reached by subtracting structure from somewhere. The negation line therefore complements rather than duplicates Pizzi's three. Second, Pizzi's three reductios establish ¬◇∅ at the level of the bare-existential conclusion; the present argument runs that same closure across the convergent lines of [§3.2](convergence.html#sec-3-2)–[§3.3](convergence.html#sec-3-3) (tallied at [§3.5](convergence.html#sec-3-5)) and then *names the necessary content*. The naming is what closes Pizzi's §7.

Pizzi's §7 surveys the candidates for the necessary existent his argument has established: abstracta (Platonism), substratum (priority monism), modal-realist plurality, theistic models, and Vedāntic Brahman. He notes that the argument is silent on which candidate occupies the slot, citing this silence as a virtue of the argument's neutrality. The present account agrees that the argument *to* □∃x x is silent on the slot's occupant, and disagrees that the silence is virtuous: there is a further argument to run, and §5 is where it runs.

The candidates require different verdicts. Abstracta may be coherent as abstracta; the present argument does not infer from their atemporality that they are impossible. The relevant question is whether they can ground the global domain of real possibility or the concrete, change-realizing world. That requires an additional grounding relation, and the abstracta theorist must supply its content. Priority monism may identify the cosmos as a partless whole prior to its parts. The present account can grant that priority while asking whether the whole, insofar as it realizes change and grounds configurations, instantiates the structural roles. The verdict is not that every candidate simply collapses into T∧S∧Φ, but that none receives automatic entitlement to the grounding office merely from Pizzi's □∃x x conclusion.

Modal-realist plurality supplies concrete worlds subject to Lewis's worldmate criterion. Change-rich Lewis worlds realize the structural roles, while sparse or changeless candidates remain tests for the book's independent necessity and type-level arguments; and the fictionalism line in [§3.3.3](convergence.html#sec-3-3-3) picks this up against modal fictionalism's milder cousin. Theistic models split on the classical/temporal distinction taken up at [§5.2.1](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-2-1) and [§5.3.3](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-3-3). A classical model that denies the loaded types may still posit determinate grounding or dependence roles; Chapter 5 must test whether those can remain wholly outside the structure rather than simply defining the model as ∅. Temporal, process, and open-theist models more directly instantiate the roles. Vedāntic Brahman likewise divides into nirguna and saguna readings at [§5.2.2](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-2-2); the burden is to determine whether the former is genuinely contentless or instead carries thin determinacy, while the latter more openly carries structure. In each case the structural account adds a further question Pizzi's result leaves open: does the candidate realize, ground, or merely coexist with the structural roles required by a concrete change-realizing Reality? Some candidates may be compatible abstracta or metaphysical pictures; none is selected as the necessary ground by □∃x x alone. The Chapter 5 engagements supply differentiated verdicts rather than a simple reduction of every candidate to one option.

The closing chapter of *The Impossibility of Nothingness* ([§8.3](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-3)) places Pizzi's conclusion in a theist-friendly axiological frame, citing Adams[@adams1999] on the goodness of the existence of God as the contemporary anchor for the move from "something exists necessarily" to "the necessary existent is divine." Pizzi flags this as a gesture rather than an argument, and is explicit at [§8.2](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-2) that the formal result of the book is silent on theism. The present account takes the disclaimer at face value. Already engaged at [§5.1.1](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-1-1) is the contemporary necessary-existence cluster[@prussRasmussen2018; @pizzi2025] as a methodologically continuous neighborhood that nonetheless does not reach this account's conclusion. The axiological gesture is a separate move from the modal-existence argument, and one this account does not run. T ∧ S ∧ Φ are not maximally great in the value-theoretic sense; they are necessary because nothing else is a *something*. The axiological closing is available to anyone who has reached □∃x x and wants to identify the necessary existent with a value-maximal being; the present account reaches the stronger and value-neutral □(T ∧ S ∧ Φ), and the axiological move does not gain traction on it.

*What is established.* Pizzi's dialectical placement is therefore distinctive. He sits here among the modal and semantic foundations rather than among the §5 engagements, because those sections take up positions that disagree with the present account about the *form* of the necessary ground: classical theism ([§5.2.1](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-2-1)), Swinburne's personal-God theism ([§5.1.4](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-1-4)), Spinozism ([§5.3.1](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-3-1)), Neoplatonism ([§5.3.2](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-3-2)), Plantinga's modal ontological argument ([§5.1.7](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-1-7)), and so on. Pizzi disagrees with none of the formal commitments. He runs the same kind of argument to a strictly weaker conclusion and leaves the further work undone. The reply is correspondingly cooperative: this section catalogs the convergence, names where Pizzi stops, and points to the sections that pick up the work he sets down. *Necessary Existence*[@prussRasmussen2018] shares Pizzi's bare-existential terminus and runs by formal-modal apparatus. Rasmussen's *How Reason Can Lead to God*[@rasmussen2019], engaged at [§5.1.1](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-1-1), pushes past the bare-existential terminus by stage-by-stage construction toward a personal necessary being. The cluster is the closest the contemporary literature comes to the present argument, and the gap between □∃x x and □(T ∧ S ∧ Φ) is Chapter 5's central piece of work.

### 4.1.12 Dispositionalism about Modality {#sec-4-1-12}

Dispositionalism is the nearest rival the account has, and it is nearest because it agrees with the account about the thing most other positions deny. It holds that possibility is grounded in actual reality rather than conferred by a plurality of worlds. Where @lewis1986 makes ◇p true by the existence of a concrete world at which p obtains, the dispositionalist makes ◇p true by a property of something actual: a potentiality, a power, a disposition. @vetter2015 gives the position its book-length statement, grounding modality in object-level potentialities and dispensing with worlds as explanatorily basic; @borghiniWilliams2008 and @jacobs2010 run the article-length versions; @pruss2011 develops a related actualist grounding. Behind them stands the dispositional essentialism of @bird2007 and @mumford2004, with @mumfordAnjum2011 on the causal side.

A distinction has to be drawn before the engagement starts, because two different theses travel under one name. Dispositionalism about *laws* holds that laws are the structural expressions of the dispositional essences of natural kinds. That thesis is engaged at [§2.8.1](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-1), where it is one of four law-accounts the constitutive claim survives, and the engagement there is complete. Dispositionalism about *modality* is a different and more ambitious thesis: not that laws are grounded in powers, but that ◇ itself is. It is that thesis this section takes up, and it presses at the point [§4.1.10](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-10) is defended.

The concession runs in full.
