A Kratzer-style modal base restricts the domain rather than populating it, and every subset of the global domain has only members of the global domain. The hyperintensionality complaint is conceded in full: necessary equivalence is too coarse for many metaphysical distinctions, which cuts below the necessity claim without cutting into it. Non-normal worlds are the real exception, since invalidating necessitation is a genuine way to block the lift; the reply there is redirection to the non-S5 route of [§3.5.4](convergence.html#sec-3-5-4) rather than defense. The verdict is **representational enlargement without domain enlargement, with one semantic route answered by redirection** ([§4.1.14](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-14)).

**Chained-origin counterexamples.** The tolerance chaining that generates Chisholm's paradox makes what is possible for an individual vary from world to world, which is genuine pressure on S4 and S5 and is not dismissed here. It reaches de re identity claims about contingent individuals; the structural claim is de dicto and quantifies over none. The verdict is **live pressure on a scope the argument does not occupy** ([§4.4.11](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4-11)).

**The remoteness objection.** That the modal faculty grows unreliable at metaphysical distances is granted without reservation, and then declined as beside the point, because the method it impugns is not the method in use: the book's negative results come from attempted specification and diagnosed failure, not from imaginative survey. The verdict is **the faculty conceded, the method refused, and a standard incurred** ([§4.1.13](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-13)).

#### 5. Convergence

**Pizzi's impossibility of nothingness.** Not a rival but the literature's nearest cousin: the same closure of modal space against ∅, reached by kindred reductio machinery, ending at the bare-existential □∃x x rather than the structural □(T ∧ S ∧ Φ). The verdict is **convergence at the modal floor, with the naming of the necessary content left to Chapter 5** ([§4.1.11](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-11)).

### What the pattern establishes

The chapter's positive finding is not that every objection secretly proves the full Necessity of Nature. It is more exact: no rival surveyed supplies a fully articulated alternative that both avoids the relevant structural roles and performs the work for which it was introduced. Some candidates dissolve. Many relocate roles. Several remain compatible specifications. A few remain coherent at a price or mark an explanatory question that the book carries forward.

The claim remains falsifiable. A genuine defeater would specify a real ground, world, or change-realizer that performs its stated work while instantiating none of the relevant roles, without merely appealing to primitive exemption or shifting to a different relative modality. Producing such a case would defeat the corresponding structural claim. None of the positions considered here has done so.

What counts as having failed to produce one is now fixed rather than left to judgment. The Specification Test ([§4.1.13](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-13)) holds that a failure to specify is evidence of impossibility only where the failure is diagnosed — where the attempt can be shown to deploy what it denies — and not where the attempt merely stalls. The test binds this ledger as much as it binds the rivals: any verdict above that rests on a failure encountered rather than exhibited is owed a downgrade, not a defense.

The chapter therefore ends without a victory lap. It leaves a ledger: structural absence fails where it is supposed to describe a world; relocation does not displace the roles; compatibility does not amount to refutation; explanatory cost is not incoherence; a restriction cannot manufacture a member, and a doubt about the faculty is not a defeat of the method; convergence at the floor is not the structural conclusion; and open seams remain open until the chapters that bear them do their work.
